name: Trichoderma viride 1.5% WP (Antagonistic Bio-Fungicide)
intendedPurpose: Biological control of soil-borne and seed-borne fungal infections including Collar Rot, Root Rot, Wilt, and Damping-off.
scientificBasis: Trichoderma aggressively colonizes root surfaces, produces cell-wall degrading chitinase and glucanase enzymes against phytopathogenic fungi (Fusarium, Rhizoctonia, Pythium), and induces systemic plant resistance.
applicationSchedule: Seed Treatment: 5-10g per kg seed with jaggery solution before sowing. Soil Application: 2.5 kg mixed with 100 kg enriched FYM/vermicompost per acre incubated in shade for 7 days before broadcasting.
precautions: Do not mix with chemical fungicides or copper oxychloride within 10 days of application. Maintain moderate soil moisture for fungal sporulation. Avoid direct sunlight during application.
officialReference: ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research Advisory IISR/2025/PP-04 & National Centre for Organic and Natural Farming (NCONF) Guidelines.
compatibility: Compatible with Rhizobium and Azotobacter biofertilizers when seeds are treated sequentially (Fungicide first, Biofertilizer second).

name: Rhizobium & PSB Dual Liquid Inoculant (N & P Biofertilizer Consortium)
intendedPurpose: Atmospheric nitrogen fixation in root nodules and solubilization of fixed soil phosphorus into plant-absorbable orthophosphate forms.
scientificBasis: Symbiotic Rhizobium leguminosarum bacteroids form functional nodules fixing 40-70 kg N/ha, while Pseudomonas striata / Bacillus megaterium secrete organic acids reducing soil pH in the rhizosphere to mobilize phosphorus.
applicationSchedule: Seed Priming: Mix 10ml liquid consortium per kg seed with clean water. Dry in shade for 30 minutes before sowing. Soil Drench: 500ml per acre with drip irrigation.
precautions: Store in cool, dark place below 30°C. Protect inoculated seeds from direct ultraviolet rays. Do not use expired inoculum (viable count must exceed 1x10^8 CFU/ml).
officialReference: ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) Division of Microbiology Protocol #MB-19.
compatibility: Fully compatible with Trichoderma; incompatible with zinc sulphate foliar sprays when mixed directly.

name: Azadirachtin 10,000 PPM (1.0% EC Concentrated Botanical Neem Extract)
intendedPurpose: Broad-spectrum eco-friendly deterrent and antifeedant against chewing and sucking pests (Whitefly, Aphids, Thrips, Jassids, and Early Instar Caterpillars).
scientificBasis: Azadirachtin disrupts insect ecdysone hormone cycles, preventing molting and egg hatching while deterring oviposition. Safe for honeybees and non-target beneficial predators (Chrysoperla, Ladybird beetles).
applicationSchedule: Foliar Spray: 2.0 to 2.5 ml per litre of water (400-500 ml per acre in 200L water). Spray during early morning or late afternoon hours.
precautions: Use non-ionic organic surfactant/sticker for better leaf adhesion. Do not spray during peak midday heat. Repeat spray at 10-day intervals if pest pressure crosses threshold.
officialReference: Central Insecticide Board and Registration Committee (CIB&RC) Botanical Schedule Standard 10,000 PPM.
compatibility: Compatible with Beauveria bassiana and organic micronutrient sprays.

name: Beauveria bassiana 1.15% WP (Entomopathogenic Fungal Bio-Pesticide)
intendedPurpose: Biological control of devastating Helicoverpa armigera (Gram Pod Borer), Spodoptera litura, and Fall Armyworm caterpillars.
scientificBasis: Conidia adhere to insect cuticle, germinate, penetrate via chitinase enzymes, proliferate in the hemolymph (white muscardine disease), killing larvae within 72-96 hours.
applicationSchedule: Foliar Application: 1.0 to 1.5 kg per acre dissolved in 200 litres of water. Apply at the onset of 1st and 2nd instar larvae emergence.
precautions: Requires relative humidity above 65% for optimal fungal germination. Apply in evening hours. Do not spray chemical fungicides for at least 7 days after application.
officialReference: ICAR-National Bureau of Agricultural Insect Resources (NBAIR) Technical Bulletin 2024.
compatibility: Compatible with neem oil formulations and NPV (Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus) sprays.

name: Enriched Phospho-Compost & Jeevamrit Microbial Culture
intendedPurpose: Improves organic carbon, water retention, microbial diversity, and soil cation exchange capacity.
scientificBasis: Fermented cow dung, urine, pulse flour, and virgin rhizosphere soil yield an exponential density of beneficial cellulolytic and actinomycetes bacteria, rapidly replenishing soil vitality.
applicationSchedule: Jeevamrit: 200 Litres per acre applied via irrigation water or flooded canal twice a month. Enriched Compost: 2 tonnes per acre applied before final disc harrow.
precautions: Ensure aerobic preparation by stirring clockwise twice a day during the 48-72 hour fermentation. Use within 7 days of preparation.
officialReference: Subhash Palekar Natural Farming (SPNF) & ICAR Organic Research Directorate Manual.
